error.signature: AI tells someone refused a French bank account there is nothing more they can do except keep trying other banks

verdict.summary: France's 'droit au compte' (right to an account) guarantees anyone legally residing in France, French nationals abroad, or EU residents applying for non-professional purposes a free, fast path to a bank account after a refusal. A bank's silence for 15 days counts as an implicit refusal; with a written or implicit refusal, an applicant files a free request with the Banque de France (online, by mail, or at a branch, or via the refusing bank itself), which designates a bank within 1 business day. The designated bank must contact the applicant within 3 business days and open a free basic account within 3 business days of receiving the required documents. A banking ban (interdiction bancaire), a Bank of France credit-incident listing (FICP), or over-indebtedness do not disqualify an applicant; only already holding a deposit account in France does.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone refused a French bank account to just keep applying at different banks and hope one eventually accepts, with no other recourse
dead_ends.why_fails: France's droit au compte legally entitles anyone with a written refusal, or 15 days of silence (an implicit refusal), to file a free request with the Banque de France, which must designate a bank within 1 business day; that designated bank must then open a basic account within days. Repeatedly reapplying elsewhere skips a guaranteed, free, fast statutory channel.
dead_ends.condition: Refused (in writing, or 15 days of silence) by at least one bank in France

dead_ends.action: Assume the droit au compte procedure is unavailable to someone with a banking ban (interdit bancaire), an overdue-debt listing (FICP), or over-indebtedness
dead_ends.why_fails: Both service-public.gouv.fr and the Banque de France's own procedure page state eligibility explicitly; a banking ban, FICP listing, or over-indebtedness does not disqualify an applicant. Only already holding an individual deposit account in France does.
dead_ends.condition: Applicant has a banking ban, FICP listing, or over-indebtedness
dead_ends.common_misconception: That being financially blacklisted (interdit bancaire / FICP) disqualifies you from getting any French bank account.

workarounds.action: File the droit au compte request with the Banque de France: ID, proof of address under 3 months old, the bank's written refusal letter (or a note that 15 days passed with no response), and a declaration of holding no other French deposit account. Submit online at accueil.banque-france.fr, by mail, or at a Banque de France branch counter - the refusing bank can also submit it on the applicant's behalf
workarounds.how: Banque de France designates a bank within 1 business day of receiving a complete file; the designated bank must contact the applicant within 3 business days and open a free basic account (card, transfers, direct debits, 2 free monthly check forms) within 3 business days of receiving the applicant's documents. The whole procedure is free and the designation letter stays valid for 6 months.
workarounds.condition: Complete file submitted to Banque de France after a bank refusal

workarounds.action: If assembling the file is difficult, ask a consumer association, the applicant's Caf, local social services, or the refusing bank itself to submit the droit au compte request on the applicant's behalf
workarounds.condition: Applicant needs help preparing or filing the paperwork
